what_is_wrong_or_confirmed: The TTD step is far worse than recorded. Line 313 tests `m in decrease_expr_MOA` against an all-lowercase list with no case folding, and the current TTD drug-target file writes MOA capitalised. So 45,449 of 45,453 TTD rows (99.99 %) would be encoded `+` (activation): 29,740 `Inhibitor`, 3,555 `Antagonist`, 237 `Blocker`, 205 `Blocker (channel blocker)`, 63 `Replacement`, 19 `Degrader` and so on. Only 4 lowercase rows come out `-`. In practice NORDic turns TTD inhibitors into activators. The producer missed this because its reproduction built the TTD cache by applying line 313 to lowercase synthetic strings (conversion_defect.md caveat 1).
evidence: TTD P1-07-Drug-TargetMapping.xlsx downloaded 2026-11-03 from ttd.idrblab.cn (1,194,236 B, sha256 f398fbb3c683...), column D `MOA` tabulated: exact-match `-` 4 rows, case-insensitive match 33,650 rows. NORDic main get_drug_targets.py lines 312-313 (sha256 b7c5ca7e734a...).
suggested_correction: Add this to conversion_defect.md as defect 0 (it is the most consequential), and add a capitalised `Inhibitor` row to the unit test. Reject NORDic's drug-target aggregator outright. Do not merely WATCH it.

suggested_correction: Sort ties by name (key=(-phase, name)) and regenerate results_p4 and results_s5. Until then, any byte-equality claim on the v1 handoff is luck.
